cards.text: Jesus has another story, and this one is for His disciples. A rich man has a manager, and that manager gets accused of wasting his master's possessions. Friend, that is the one email from the boss you do NOT want to open.

cards.question: The rich man calls in the manager who's been accused of wasting his possessions. What does he tell him?

answers.text: Turn in an account because you cannot be manager any longer
Pay back everything you wasted by the end of the week
Take a smaller job until you earn back my trust

cards.text: The manager talks it over with himself: “What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position?” I KNOW that feeling, friend: one day you're on the counter, the next you're in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: As he thinks about losing his position, the manager decides he can make a living by digging or begging.

cards.text: Digging? He says he's too weak. Begging? Too ashamed. Then, LIGHTBULB: “I know what I will do…”

cards.question: The manager comes up with a plan for after he's removed from his job. What's the plan for?

answers.text: So people will welcome him into their homes
So his master will give him the job back
So he can pay off his own debts

cards.text: So he calls in each of his master's debtors, and the first one owes a hundred measures of olive oil. The man is losing his job and he is STILL working the phones. Look at him GO.

cards.question: The first debtor owes the master a hundred measures of olive oil. What does the manager tell him to do with his bill?

answers.text: Sit down quickly and write fifty
Pay the full hundred by tomorrow
Double the amount to two hundred

cards.question: The next debtor owes a hundred measures of wheat. The manager tells him to take his bill and write ___.

cards.text: Two bills, two big markdowns, all on his way OUT the door. Then the master finds out, and friend, I am bracing for the explosion.

cards.question: The master finds out what his manager did with the debtors' bills. How does the master respond?

answers.text: He commends him for acting shrewdly
He has him thrown into prison
He makes him repay the difference

cards.text: COMMENDED?! The text still calls him the dishonest manager, but he's commended because he acted shrewdly. I once got a compliment from Mother Miller for a cookie I stamped upside down, so I'm trying not to judge.

cards.question: Then comes a comparison: the sons of light are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than the sons of this age are.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “I tell you,” and He starts talking about worldly wealth. Paychecks, bills, that one subscription you forgot you were paying for. That stuff.

cards.question: Remember how the manager used his master's bills? Jesus tells His disciples to use worldly wealth for what?

answers.text: To build bigger barns for themselves
To store up treasure for themselves

cards.question: Jesus says that when worldly wealth is gone, those friends will welcome them into eternal dwellings.

cards.text: There's that word again: welcome, same as in the manager's plan. Then Jesus talks about being faithful with very little and with much, and all I can picture is one cookie next to a whole cookie box.

cards.question: Jesus says someone who is dishonest with very little can still be trusted to be honest with much.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks two questions back to back, and both are about trust. It's the boss who won't hand you the building keys while you're still losing the stapler.

cards.question: Jesus asks: if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will trust you with what?
Jesus' second question: if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your ___?

cards.text: Then Jesus lands it: “No servant can serve two masters.” I tried answering two oven timers at the same time once, and I stamped my own hat.

cards.question: Jesus says a servant with two masters will end up loving both of them the same.
Jesus ends by naming two masters you cannot serve both of. Which two?
